matters.title: 6. Consider a request from Yuba County Office of Emergency Services for a Bill Shaw grant in the amount of $7,500 for a project to upgrade the PA system in the Main Exhibit Hall at the Yuba Sutter Fairgrounds. (Est. Time: 5 Min.)
matters.body: Board of Director's Regular Meeting 9:00 A.M.
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jul 16, 2024 - Board of Director's Regular Meeting 9:00 A.M. 
 Category 
 DISCUSSION ITEMS 
 Subject 
 6. Consider a request from Yuba County Office of Emergency Services for a Bill Shaw grant in the amount of $7,500 for a project to upgrade the PA system in the Main Exhibit Hall at the Yuba Sutter Fairgrounds. (Est. Time: 5 Min.) 
 Type 

 Staff Summary 

 Yuba County has an Agreement for Professional Services with the Yuba-Sutter Fairgrounds that allows Yuba County to use the Fairgrounds, including the Main Exhibit Hall, to provide care and shelter for displaced residents during a disaster response. 

 The Yuba County Office of Emergency Services (OES) utilizes the Main Exhibit Hall as a congregated shelter during all emergencies requiring the evacuation of residents. This includes flooding and high-water emergencies that may displace unhoused residents living near the river systems. However, during a training exercise held by the Health and Human Services department in the hall, it was noted that the lack of an adequate sound system had a negative impact on the hall's usability. 

 This project is a collaboration between the Yuba City Rotary, Yuba-Sutter Fairgrounds, Hlbers, and Yuba County OES. The Yuba County Water Agency Bill Shaw grant request to Yuba Water for $7,500 would cover the remaining amount needed for the project. 

 However, the $7,500 grant will only be paid out to Yuba County OES once the rest of the funding is secured. When this happens, Yuba County will provide the Yuba-Sutter Fairgrounds or Rotary with the $7,500 so that they can purchase the necessary materials. The 2025 installation date is determined by Rotary District Policy, which makes the funding available in 2025. 

 Attachments

 Type 

 Staff Summary and Background 
 In October 2020, the Board adopted a Community Impact Grant and Loan Program Policy (policy) to guide investment in community projects within Yuba Water's mission areas. Six grant program areas were identified for investment: Flood Risk Reduction; Water Supply and Management; Watershed Resilience; Water Conservation; Water Education; and Bill Shaw Rescue Equipment and Training. The policy also outlined the process for grant application and identified two grant application windows open annually in March and September. 

 On June 4, 2024 , the Board adopted an amendment to the Community Impact Grant and Loan Program Policy (Policy) to limit certain grant and loan requests that are not associated with an external grant application to only be considered during an annual funding request window of February 1 to March 31. IRWMP related grants associated with external grant applications may be submitted at any time. 

 Recommendation 
 Upon review of the attached applications, staff determined they have merit based on their nexus to projects in progress and for services to the public and therefore warrant the committee's consideration. 

 Attachment A is a summary chart of all the grant applications recommended for approval for the March 2025 grant application window. The total of the grants recommended for approval is approximately $619,765.

matters.body: Board of Director's Regular Meeting 9:00 A.M.
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Sep 16, 2025 - Board of Director's Regular Meeting 9:00 A.M. 
 Category 
 DISCUSSION ITEMS 
 Subject 
 15. Consider approval of a legal services agreement with Hanson Bridgett LP for special counsel legal services for public works construction. 
 Type 

 Staff Summary 
 With a number of significant approved and potential construction projects planned, Agency legal counsel identified a need for additional special counsel support from experienced public works construction counsel. In April 2025, the Agency requested qualifications from nine law firms. In June 2025, a selection team including representatives from Agency Legal, Power Systems, Resource Planning, and Finance interviewed three law firms and conducted reference checks. 

 The selection team identified the construction team at the law firm Hanson Bridgett as the preferred team. The firm team of Joseph Moore, P.E., Allison Schutte, and David Gehrig have decades of experience assisting public agencies with public works construction matters, including contracting, alternative delivery, contractor issues and claims, and litigation. Industry honors for the firms' construction practice include a top-tier ranking from Chambers USA, indicating that the firm's construction practice is considered among the top three in California. 

 Agency staff expect to engage Hanson Bridgett on an as-needed basis for the Colgate Tunnel Outage project, the Nature-Like Fishway, and future projects like the proposed ARC Spillway project. 

 Agency staff request approval of the proposed legal services agreement and direction to the General Manager to execute the agreement. 

 Fiscal Impact 
 No additional fiscal impact to the FY26 budget is anticipated. Legal services will be used on an as-needed basis consistent with the existing Agency budget line items for public works construction projects. 

 Prior Board Action 
 None 

 Strategic Plan Component 
 Strategic Priority #5: Further develop Yuba Water's organizational capabilities to efficiently support operations. Objective #4: Further develop the structure and support tools to provide operational effectiveness and efficiency to power systems, water resources, and all Yuba Water operations. 

 Attachments 
 A- Draft Hanson Bridgett Legal Services Agreement

Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jun 16, 2026 - Board of Director's Regular Meeting 10:00 A.M. 
 Category 
 DISCUSSION ITEMS 
 Subject 
 4. Consider approval of the review and revisions to the following Board policies: 1) Staff Interaction Policy (non-substantial changes), 2) Training Policy (formally Director Harassment Prevention Training Policy), 3) Directors’ Compensation and Expense Reimbursement Policy, 4) Policy Concerning Ethics, General Manager, and Related Matters, 5) Rules for Proceedings of the Board of Directors Policy, and 7) Drug Free Workplace Policy (removing). 
 Type 

 Staff Report 
 Yuba Water Agency’s (Yuba Water) Board policies are reviewed regularly to ensure they remain current, consistent with applicable laws, and aligned with organizational practices. Staff have completed their review of the policies scheduled for this cycle and is presenting proposed updates for Board consideration. 

 Discussion 
 The Staff Interaction Policy had no substantive revisions, only minor formatting changes were made to improve clarity and consistency with Yuba Water’s branding guide. 

 The Training Policy, formally the Director Harassment Prevention Training Policy, has been updated to include all the legislative mandated trainings required for Board members. The revisions incorporate ethics training (formally included in the Policy Concerning Ethics, General Manager, and Related Matters) and add new fiscal and finance training required by Senate Bill 827 (SB 827) that went into effect in October of 2025. Rather than maintaining separate policies for each required training, all mandatory training requirements have been consolidated into a single policy. 

 The Directors’ Compensation and Expense Reimbursement Policy was updated to reflect current compensation levels and reimbursement rates. 

 The Policy Concerning Ethics, General Manager, and Related Matters was revised to remove the ethics training component, as that requirement is now fully addressed within the Training Policy as discussed above. The policy was also revised to reflect Agency existing practice that the Finance Director is appointed by the General Manager, but the Board sets policy for the management and transparency of Agency finances. No other changes were made to this policy. 

 The Rules for Proceedings of the Board of Directors Policy have been updated to comply with the requirements of Senate Bill 707 (SB 707), ensuring that Board procedures are consistent with current statutory obligations. 

 The Drug Free Workplace Policy is recommended for removal because its requirements are already addressed in the Human Resources policies “Drug and Alcohol Use Policy” and “Drug and Alcohol Policy for DOT Covered Positions”. As a result, a separate Board policy is no longer necessary. 

 Staff recommends that the Board approve the revised policies, acknowledge the reviewed policies, and approve the removal of the obsolete policies.
